searchText: <@425572898787426305> I didn't get your last message 😄 (zoom cut off before I could read it) IMO, it makes sense to have that max reorg depth constant defining the min block retention period as well i.e. EL client should retain blocks for at least `REORG_RETENTION_WINDOW` Ah I see, copying from zoom: I think the argument was that the reorg depth constant is related to the inactivity leak whereas the cl block retention policy is related to the wsp I _do_ think we can make it the same though and just note that it implies some safety decay constant. But also just to clarify, I handwaved my way to 8192 epochs based on operational overhead 😄 which was a coincidence one month would imply something like safety decay = ~20 I think i am wondering if blocks could become necessery to recover from a long period of non-finality by any means 🤔 Was going through all the edge cases and ended up noting that for periods of long non-finality, the node should probably hold onto those unfinalised blocks 😄 This means we decouple historical block serving for checkpoint sync from non-finality related recovery mechanisms It was a wall of text so I wont paste it here, but one edge case I was not able to think through is what happens when a node rejoins the network after 50 days of non-finality (they were offline for the whole 50 days, so they cannot use their local fork-choice data to help them recover) (It seems that for these very edge casey scenarios, the main solution is to get a checkpoint from an externally trusted source, though admittedly I haven't thought a lot about this) Created this: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12188/changes Added a note on long periods of finality
